candidates.cover_letter:
Dear AWA People & Culture Team,

I’m writing to join AWA’s Talent Network because your work sits exactly where my experience and my heart meet: helping young people and their families through some of the hardest moments of their lives.

For more than 25 years, I have designed and facilitated learning programs, coached leaders and individuals, and coordinated group programs in person and online, in English and in Spanish. Early in my career in Venezuela, I co-facilitated a community prevention program for adolescents sponsored by Empresas Polar, with workshops on substance use and teen pregnancy prevention for teens living near the company’s facilities. That experience showed me how much prevention depends on reaching families in their own language and reality.

This work is also personal. Addiction to alcohol and drugs has touched my own family, and I have lost a young family member to its consequences. I now have four young grandchildren, and the idea of contributing to prevention efforts that protect children like them means a great deal to me.

I believe I could add value to AWA by supporting staff training and onboarding, developing educational workshops for families, especially Spanish-speaking families, or helping coordinate programs so that teens and parents stay engaged and informed. I’m based in Miami, fully bilingual, and comfortable working remotely or on-site in Miami.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the chance to learn how I could support your team and the families you serve.

Warm regards,
Esther Leon
(713) 504-7640 · leoncesther@gmail.com · linkedin.com/in/esther-leon-ld

Dear AWA People & Culture team,

I first came across Adolescent Wellness Academy through a job post. With a bit of research, I found it to be a beloved program that changed many young lives for the better. As a creative professional with a growing interest in psychology and a wish to work with the younger crowd, I made a note to myself: Reach out. With my help as a social media professional, we can share your story, multiply the healing impact and foster deeper connections with the local community.

As a digital storyteller, I have spent the last decade sharpening my tools, working in all facets of content production from concept development to polished delivery with a brand-tailored, mission-aligned strategic foundation. At Little’s Photography, I worked closely with hundreds of high-schoolers as a fine-art senior portrait photographer and photo editor, while producing an extensive promotional video library for the studio’s marketing initiatives. Our promos reached thousands of clients and led to a surge in the sales of photoshoot packages. I produced organic social content for the Columbia College Chicago Student Communications IG feed, and filmed interview-based documentaries that were showcased all across the university campus. With consistent hard-work as a freelancer, one of my long-time remote clients Emel Onur now has 47,500+ followers on her YouTube channel, compared to the 50 followers we started our journey with.

More recently, I helped establish an Instagram account that is dear to me. My teenage cousin Kağan has a rare form of epilepsy called Dravet Syndrome. Against all odds, he joined the Turkish national tennis team in the special needs category. My aunt was inspired to share their story, so we can build a community and reach those who can help Kağan access the treatment he needs. In the last 3 months, our engagement surged and we got more than 200,000 views. More importantly, we connected with people in very meaningful ways and networked with a foundation who wants to conduct research to find the right treatment. It makes me very happy to be able to have a positive effect on my family and community in Turkey from thousands of miles away.

What excites me the most about the prospect of joining your team is that I wholeheartedly share the aspiration to provide a safe space for teens, where they feel loved and cared for, so we water the seeds of healing for generations to come. I’d appreciate the chance to discuss how I can contribute to your mission. You can reach me at 561-409-6908 or idilmeric@hotmail.com. Thank you for your time—I look forward to hearing from you.

Warm regards,
Idil Meric

I am writing to express my interest in the Program Operations position within your adolescent mental health PHP/IOP program. With approximately 12 years of experience working with individuals with autism, behavioral challenges, and social-emotional needs, I bring a strong foundation in behavioral support, staff training, leadership, and program structure. My professional background has allowed me to develop a thorough understanding of what it takes to create safe, consistent, and supportive environments for both clients and staff.

My experience began at Ramapo for Children, where I worked in several capacities, including lifeguard, swim instructor, and Toolbox Specialist. During my time there, I worked closely with neurodiverse individuals and those with behavioral and emotional challenges. As a Toolbox Specialist, I developed and implemented individualized behavioral strategies, problem-solved challenging situations, and trained other staff members on how to effectively respond to and manage difficult behaviors. This experience helped establish my leadership skills and taught me the importance of staff development, consistency, and individualized support.

Over the years, I have continued to build on that foundation through my work as a Registered Behavior Technician. I have approximately four years of experience implementing behavior intervention plans, collecting and analyzing behavioral data, collaborating with BCBAs, and maintaining strong relationships with clients and their families. I have worked with children and adolescents with varying levels of behavioral and communication needs, including individuals who require significant support with emotional regulation and challenging behaviors.

Beyond my direct clinical experience, I consider myself a natural leader who values accountability, teamwork, and clear communication. I have experience training and guiding staff, modeling appropriate interventions, and helping others develop the skills and confidence needed to work effectively with challenging populations. I understand that successful programs depend on more than clinical services alone. They require organized daily operations, effective communication, staff coordination, accurate documentation, strong safety practices, and the ability to adapt when unexpected challenges arise.

I am particularly interested in this opportunity because it would allow me to combine my behavioral health experience with my leadership abilities and passion for working with adolescents. While my background has primarily been in direct service, it has given me firsthand insight into the operational challenges staff face and the systems necessary to maintain a successful program. Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

I am writing to express my interest in joining the Adolescent Wellness Academy team in Boca Raton. Your mission to provide adolescents with a safe, supportive environment where they feel seen, understood, and genuinely cared for deeply resonates with both my personal values and professional purpose.

As a board-certified Health and Wellness Coach, Hypnotherapist, and Fitness Instructor, I bring a holistic approach to physical, mental, and emotional well-being. My work focuses on helping individuals develop healthier habits, manage stress, build self-awareness, strengthen emotional resilience, and create positive, sustainable changes in their lives.

I strongly believe that the foundations of overall wellness should be taught from an early age. Equipping adolescents with practical tools for emotional regulation, stress management, mindfulness, healthy habits, and self-awareness can better prepare them to navigate the challenges of life and an increasingly demanding world. These are invaluable life skills that can positively influence their well-being well into adulthood.

As a mother, I also appreciate the unique pressures adolescents face today and the importance of having compassionate, trustworthy individuals who can support and guide them through this formative stage of life.

I believe my background in health and mindset coaching, behavior change, mindfulness, breathwork, and nervous system regulation would complement AWA’s multidisciplinary approach. I bring warmth, empathy, patience, and a genuine passion for empowering others to recognize their potential and develop the skills to thrive.

What particularly draws me to AWA is your commitment to seeing beyond an adolescent’s struggles and recognizing the individual within. I would love the opportunity to collaborate with your team and contribute to an organization that shares my belief in nurturing the whole person.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my qualifications, experience, and passion for holistic well-being could contribute to your team and make a meaningful difference in the lives of the adolescents and families you serve.

Warm regards,

Christina Samuda

candidates.cover_letter:
November 25, 2026

Hiring Team Adolescent Wellness Academy Boca Raton, FL

Re: Creative Group Facilitator – Adolescent Mental Health

Dear AWA Hiring Team,

I'm excited to apply for the Creative Group Facilitator role. I'm a K–8 art teacher with a B.A. in Studio Art and Psychology from Florida State University, and I'm currently earning my M.S. in Clinical Mental Health Counseling at Walden University. I've spent my career at the point where art, behavior and emotional growth meet. Helping teens build confidence and coping skills through creative work is exactly the kind of work I want to be doing.

Leading groups with adolescents. 
I teach art to students in kindergarten through 8th grade, including middle schoolers on the edge of the age group AWA serves. Every day I plan and lead hands-on lessons that work for students with very different skill levels, attention spans and comfort with being creative in front of peers. I created a tiered behavior escalation framework for my classroom, so I can handle tough group moments calmly and consistently while keeping the room safe for everyone. After my first year, I built a full curriculum by hand, planned month by month so lessons build on each other and stay fresh.

Adapting creative work to each person. 
As a Clinical Educator at Cayer Behavioral Group, an ABA practice, I worked with K–5 children with autism. I used each child's data to design sensory-friendly, hands-on activities tailored to their needs. I worked alongside the clinical team and advocated for the kids, especially around their feelings. Earlier, as a nanny, I ran "Creative Play" sessions with short art lessons built into each child's care plan. I've learned that the activity is only the vehicle. What matters is whether each participant feels safe enough to try.

A clinical lens. 
My psychology coursework at FSU included abnormal psychology, neurodivergence and neuroscience. At Walden, I'm studying counseling techniques and trauma-informed care. In a PHP or IOP setting, that helps me understand what teens may be carrying into the room. It also helps me know when to invite expression and when to give space, and how to document what I see in a way that's useful to the clinical team. I'm used to timely documentation from tracking student progress data and keeping records in my school's gradebook system.

My own creative background goes beyond the classroom.
It includes studio art, commissioned signage work and clarinet performance, so I can offer a range of expressive activities, from drawing and collage to music and mindful making. I'd love to bring that range, along with real care for teens, to your village.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I'd welcome the chance to talk about how I could support AWA's creative programming.

Sincerely,

Justine Therrien

October 28, 2026

Hiring Manager
Adolescent Wellness Academy

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in joining the team at Adolescent Wellness Academy. With hands-on experience in youth development, art instruction, creative education, and community programming, I am excited about the opportunity to contribute to an environment dedicated to supporting adolescents’ well-being, personal development, and growth.

My experience working with children and teens through the Boys & Girls Club and the Billy Thompson Foundation Youth Summer Camp has strengthened my appreciation for the importance of creating positive, structured, and encouraging environments where young people can develop confidence, explore their strengths, and express themselves constructively. Through art instruction and guided creative workshops, I have facilitated activities that incorporate painting, storytelling, imagination, and self-expression to encourage creativity, personal growth, and meaningful engagement.

In 2025, I served as an art instructor for the Billy Thompson Foundation Youth Summer Camp, delivering structured art workshops for children and teenagers. I also led a community painting experience at JPP International Church through Painting With A Twist, facilitating an engaging group activity for approximately 40 participants. Earlier in my career, my work with the Boys & Girls Club involved youth art programming designed to encourage imagination, confidence, and self-expression. These experiences have reinforced my belief that young people benefit from opportunities to discover their abilities, develop positive relationships, and engage in activities that promote healthy self-expression.

I currently serve as Program Coordinator for Paint With Purpose, a community arts and creative wellness initiative that uses guided painting experiences to encourage self-expression, confidence, healing, and connection. My responsibilities include developing and coordinating creative workshops, planning activities, preparing materials, communicating with participants, and exploring partnerships with community organizations and schools. This work reflects my commitment to using creativity as a constructive way to bring people together and create meaningful community experiences.

In addition to my experience in youth programming and the arts, I bring more than 10 years of experience in administrative support, client relations, organizational coordination, and professional communication. My background includes supporting leadership, coordinating schedules and activities, managing documentation, and handling confidential information with discretion. These skills would allow me to contribute organization, reliability, professionalism, and effective communication to your team.

I am also pursuing a Bachelor of Arts in Psychology at South Florida Bible College, with anticipated completion in 2028. My educational path complements my interest in human development, individual strengths, and the factors that contribute to personal growth and well-being. As an artist, published children’s book author, and creative educator, I am passionate about helping people recognize their potential and discover constructive ways to communicate and express themselves. My CPR and AED certification, obtained in 2023, further reflects my commitment to maintaining relevant practical skills.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, creativity, compassion, and organizational strengths to Adolescent Wellness Academy. I am particularly interested in contributing to a supportive environment where adolescents are encouraged to develop healthy coping strategies, build confidence, strengthen interpersonal skills, and recognize their capacity for growth. I would be proud to contribute to a team that approaches youth development with professionalism, respect, consistency, and an understanding of the importance of individualized support.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background in youth development, creative programming, psychology studies, and professional administration could contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy and its mission.

Sincerely,

Shamaiah Manriquez

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear AWA Academy Team,

I am so excited to apply for the opportunity to join AWA Academy’s IOP/PHP team working with adolescents. As a therapist who graduated in December 2025, I am eager to continue growing as a clinician in a setting that aligns with something I am truly passionate about: supporting children, adolescents, and their families. I am especially drawn to AWA Academy because of the impact your work has on the lives of children and families, and I would love to be part of that mission.

I currently work as an intake therapist for a virtual IOP program, where I work with both adults and children. I also have experience working in an inpatient psychiatric hospital with adults, where I facilitated group therapy and conducted intake assessments. These experiences have helped me build my clinical skills, connect with clients from different backgrounds, and better understand the importance of compassionate, individualized care.

Before becoming a therapist, I worked as a special education teacher with children on the autism spectrum. Working with children and families was one of the most meaningful parts of my professional journey and played a big role in shaping the kind of therapist I wanted to become. I genuinely love working with kids and helping them feel understood, supported, and empowered. I would love the opportunity to bring that passion into my clinical work with adolescents and their families.

My therapeutic approach incorporates concepts from ACT and DBT, and I am excited to continue building on these skills while gaining more experience in individual therapy. I am eager to learn, grow, and challenge myself as a clinician, and I would be grateful for the opportunity to do so alongside a team that shares my commitment to supporting young people through difficult moments in their lives.

I am also fluent in both English and Portuguese, which allows me to connect with and support families from different linguistic and cultural backgrounds. I currently hold a license as a Registered Mental Health Intern and have a qualified supervisor. I anticipate to become fully licensed in a year and a half.

I would be genuinely excited to join AWA Academy and contribute to the meaningful work you do with children and families. Thank you for taking the time to consider my application. I would love the opportunity to connect and share more about my experience and enthusiasm for this role!

Thank you!

Rebecca Ubertini

Bilingual Clinical Mental Health Clinician

Bilingual (English/Spanish) counselor with an MEd in Clinical Mental Health Counseling and supervised clinical training across community mental health, school, and outpatient settings. candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Therapy position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. As a Registered Clinical Social Work Intern (RCSWI), I am passionate about supporting individuals through life’s challenges and helping them develop the tools and skills necessary to achieve emotional wellness, resilience, and personal growth. I believe my clinical experience, diverse background working with various populations, and dedication to providing compassionate, client-centered care would make me a valuable addition to your team.

In my current role, I provide therapeutic services to youth, adolescents, and adults with a wide range of mental health and behavioral health needs, including PTSD, depression, anxiety, ADHD, autism, and substance use disorders. I utilize evidence-based therapeutic approaches, including Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT), and trauma-informed care, to help clients navigate challenges, strengthen coping skills, regulate emotions, and work toward their individualized treatment goals. I strive to create a safe, supportive, and nonjudgmental therapeutic environment where clients feel heard, respected, and empowered throughout their healing journey.

In addition to my clinical experience, I have worked with diverse and vulnerable populations, including individuals impacted by domestic violence, substance use, homelessness, disabilities, and challenges associated with aging. These experiences have strengthened my ability to approach each individual with empathy, patience, cultural sensitivity, and an understanding of the unique circumstances that influence mental health and overall well-being. I recognize the importance of meeting clients where they are, building trusting therapeutic relationships, and tailoring interventions to their individual needs and strengths.

I am a driven, hardworking, compassionate, and dedicated professional who values collaboration, continued learning, and professional growth. I am committed to helping clients recognize their strengths, overcome barriers, and build healthier, more fulfilling lives. I am particularly interested in the opportunity to contribute my skills and passion to Adolescent Wellness Academy and support the emotional and psychological well-being of the individuals and families served by your organization.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical experience, therapeutic approach, and commitment to quality mental health care align with the needs of your team. I look forward to the possibility of contributing to the important work being done at Adolescent Wellness Academy.

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Relief Nursery Hiring Committee,

I am excited to apply for the Early Childhood Skills Trainer position. With a bachelor's degree in Neuroscience and Pre-Med, professional experience as a Qualified Mental Health Associate and Registered Behavior Technician, and a background in behavioral health, childcare, and residential treatment, I bring a strong foundation in child development, behavioral intervention, and trauma-informed, family-centered care. I am particularly drawn to Relief Nursery's commitment to early intervention and its recognition of the importance of creating safe, supportive environments during a child's formative years.

Throughout my professional experience, I have worked with children and individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities, behavioral challenges, mental health conditions, and complex support needs as well as multiple diagnoses. As a Registered Behavior Technician, I developed skills in implementing individualized behavioral interventions, supporting emotional and behavioral regulation, encouraging positive skill development, and using developmentally appropriate approaches to promote independence and healthy relationships in a pediatric setting. My additional childcare and tutoring experience has strengthened my ability to connect with children at different developmental stages, adapt my approach to individual and family needs, and create engaging, supportive learning environments.

My experience in behavioral health and residential rehabilitation has also provided me with a strong understanding of trauma-informed care, crisis intervention, de-escalation, and the importance of consistency and positive relationship-building. I have collaborated with multidisciplinary teams, communicated with families and caregivers, maintained documentation, and supervised and trained staff in residential settings. These experiences have taught me the importance of approaching challenging behaviors with patience and curiosity, recognizing that behavior is often a form of communication and that children benefit most from environments where they feel safe, understood, and supported.

What particularly interests me about Relief Nursery is the chance to make a meaningful difference through early intervention. I believe that providing children with the emotional regulation, communication, and social skills they need at an early age can have a lasting impact on their development and future success. I would welcome the opportunity to work alongside teachers, therapists, families, and other professionals to support each child's individual goals while strengthening family relationships and promoting resilience.

I would be excited to bring my educational background, behavioral health experience, compassion, and dedication to child development to the Relief Nursery team. Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience and qualifications align with your program's needs.

Sincerely,  
Anne Bradford

Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. I am currently pursuing a degree in Business Administration at Mississippi State University on the pre-nursing track, and I am eager to combine my passion for helping others with my experience in customer service and healthcare administration.

With over four years of customer service experience, I have developed strong communication, organization, and problem-solving skills. I also have previous experience working at the front desk of North Mississippi Urology, where I assisted with patient scheduling, answered phone calls, and supported daily office operations. These experiences have taught me the importance of patience, professionalism, and making every individual feel heard and supported.

What particularly draws me to this position is the opportunity to help adolescents and their families navigate what can be an incredibly overwhelming time in their lives. I understand how important it is for families to feel comfortable, understood, and reassured when seeking mental health or substance use treatment. I would love to be a compassionate and welcoming first point of contact for those families.

I would describe myself as friendly, empathetic, dependable, and highly coachable. I learn quickly, enjoy connecting with people, and take pride in staying organized while managing multiple responsibilities. As a small business owner, I have also developed strong independent working skills, time management, and accountability, which I believe would translate well into a virtual position.

My upcoming coursework is entirely online, allowing me greater flexibility and the ability to dedicate myself to this role. I am genuinely excited about the opportunity to grow within the healthcare field while contributing to an organization that makes a meaningful difference in the lives of young people and their families.

Thank you so much for considering my application. I would love the opportunity to speak with you further and learn how I could contribute to your team.

Best,  
Katie Thomas

candidates.cover_letter:
Cover Letter – Adolescent Wellness Admissions Coordinator

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to express my interest in the Adolescent Wellness Admissions Coordinator position. Throughout my career, I have developed a strong passion for helping individuals feel heard, supported, and empowered to take the next steps toward their personal goals. I believe my background in office management, client relations, marketing, and patient support would allow me to bring a valuable combination of organization, initiative, and compassion to your team.

My professional experience began with marketing at a young age, eventually leading me into an Office Manager position for a small LLC selling cleaning systems in Michigan. These experiences helped me develop strong communication, problem-solving, organizational, and administrative skills. I am comfortable working with a variety of software and organizational systems, and I have consistently demonstrated the ability to learn new programs and processes quickly.

Although I have not always considered myself a traditional leader, I naturally take initiative when I see an opportunity to improve a process, solve a problem, or make someone's experience better. I enjoy finding solutions, identifying areas that need attention, and taking steps to ensure things continue moving forward.

One of the most rewarding aspects of my current role is building relationships with clients and helping them work toward meaningful progress. I take pride in getting to know the individuals I work with, establishing trust, and creating an environment where they feel comfortable being themselves. My manager and previous directors have repeatedly recognized my ability to make patients feel at ease, regardless of their experiences or circumstances. I strive to meet people where they are, understand what they need, and work alongside them to develop a plan for what comes next.

I understand that people do not always come into a situation knowing exactly what they want or how to get there. Sometimes, the first step is simply helping them feel comfortable enough to explore their options. In my current position, I regularly coordinate meetings and develop plans with clients to identify needs, address concerns, establish goals, and ensure that we are making measurable progress. I find fulfillment in helping people recognize their potential while respecting that meaningful change has to be something they are ready and willing to pursue.

I have professional experience working with individuals ages 15 and older, and I also have a personal appreciation for working with younger populations. Throughout high school and part of middle school, I volunteered with elementary-aged students at my school. During my final year, I even took the initiative to help coordinate school concerts despite the absence of a formal music department. I have also gained experience with Project SEARCH and WINGS, which have further contributed to my understanding of individualized support and the importance of meeting people where they are.

My interest in wellness and individualized care is also personal. I have several family members with disabilities, and I am preparing to become a caregiver for my aunt, who is fully disabled. These experiences have strengthened my appreciation for the importance of patience, advocacy, understanding, and recognizing each person's individual needs. They have reinforced my belief that people deserve to be treated with dignity and compassion, regardless of the challenges they face.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, adaptability, and genuine passion for helping others to your admissions team. I believe that creating a positive first experience can make a lasting difference, particularly for adolescents and families who may be navigating unfamiliar or difficult circumstances. I would be happy to provide professional references from my current manager, previous directors, and educators who can speak to my work ethic, initiative, and ability to connect with others.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience and approach to client care could contribute to your team.

Sincerely,

Angel Hebert

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,
I am writing to express my interest in employment opportunities within your organization. I bring several years of experience working in healthcare and long-term care, along with a strong background in resident services, leadership, documentation, care planning, and coordination. I am currently continuing my education in social work and am eager to apply my experience and education in a position where I can continue to grow professionally.
Throughout my career, I have progressed from an Activities Volunteer (during middle school and high school), to being hired as an Activities Aide after graduating high school, to being promoted to a management position as the Assistant Activities Director during college, taking on increasing levels of responsibility. I also have been the interim Life Enrichment Director multiple times, my longest time being 4 months (All due to my manager being on family leave). My experience includes completing resident intake assessments and care plans, working with MDS documentation, coordinating programs and services, leading meetings, training staff, and working with individuals with dementia, mental health diagnoses, and behavioral needs. These experiences have strengthened my communication, organization, problem-solving, and time-management skills.
In addition to my professional experience, I have educational experience, as well. I am graduating this fall with an Associates Degree, and have obtained my Certificate in Social Work and am still currently pursuing my Bachelors of Social Work and Psychology (Dual major). I am expected to graduate in Fall 2027. I plan on obtaining my masters degree, as well. Although I am a full-time student, my classes are online, so school does not affect my career. I am also an Activities Professional Certified (APC) and am CPR certified. I am dependable, compassionate, detail-oriented, and comfortable working both independently and as part of a multidisciplinary team.
My dedication to my work and education has also been recognized through several awards and achievements. Most notably, I was selected as a recipient of the Pennsylvania Healthcare Association’s 2026 Stories of Caring Award. I have also been recognized as Resident Council Appointed Employee of the Month on four occasions and Staff Appointed Employee of the Month once (we can only earn each of these once per year), earned President’s List or Dean’s List honors every semester of college, and am a member of the Psi Beta Psychology Honor Society. 
 I am also very involved in work-place committees and events. I was elected as a SEIU union delegate, I am a member of the Staff Safety Committee, a member of the Staff Recruitment & Retention Committee, and I provide pet therapy to residents and staff with my dog, Winston, every Wednesday. I also founded “The Gathering Place” at my facility, which is a room where residents can safely and independently access leisure items in-between scheduled events. The room includes a TV,  jigsaw puzzle table, board games, books, magazines, iPads, puzzle books and packets, a card-writing station, and more. 
 These accomplishments and involvement reflect the level of commitment, compassion, and professionalism I strive to bring to both my work and education. 
I have been loyal and dedicated to my current company for 11 years, beginning as a volunteer and eventually progressing into a leadership position. I made the decision to attend college online so I could take the opportunity offered to me at this company. Doing so allowed me to obtain years of healthcare experience ahead of college graduation, which sets me apart. I am incredibly grateful for the opportunities, experiences, and skills I have gained throughout my time there. However, with a heavy heart, I am ready to step outside of my comfort zone, continue growing professionally, and challenge myself in a new environment. I am excited to bring the knowledge and experience I have developed throughout my career to a new organization while continuing to learn, grow, and build upon my skills.
I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, education, and dedication to your organization. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background and skills could contribute to your team.
Sincerely,
Kaylynn Sinclair

Dear Hiring Team,

I’m excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position supporting adolescents seeking mental health and substance use treatment. I’m drawn to this role because the first call can be a difficult one for families to make. I would bring a calm, compassionate approach to those conversations and help families understand what to expect and what to do next.

In my previous role as a Referrals Specialist and Office Assistant at Ogemaw Eye Institute, I coordinated referrals, scheduled appointments, verified insurance benefits, reviewed patient records, and answered questions about coverage and costs. I regularly spoke with patients who were anxious or unsure how to move forward. Those conversations taught me to listen carefully, explain unfamiliar information in plain language, and follow through so patients knew where things stood.

I would bring that same attention to detail and empathy to virtual admissions. I’m comfortable gathering sensitive information over the phone, documenting conversations accurately, and coordinating with others to keep the process moving. As a mother of two teenagers, I also appreciate how much it matters for young people to feel heard and respected while their families are trying to find support.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience in referrals, insurance verification, and patient communication could support your admissions team and the families you serve.

Sincerely,
Chloe Moraitis

They started off drinking a decent amount of alcohol or were using substances to cope and it led to serious mental health problems. Everyone has difficulties and struggles, finding the right person to listen and support you can be hard but there is someone out there. I care about people, I care about their feelings and I am an observer, I am a listener, I love helping people and I love to see people succeed in life.

Theresa Marie Therrien
Holiday, FL · (727) 589-8192 · theresa.therrien.tm@outlook.com

Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,
I am applying for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position because it sits exactly where my experience
is strongest: being the calm, clear first voice a family hears when they are reaching out for help during a
hard moment.

For more than twenty years, my work has been built on guiding people through personal, sometimes
emotional decisions. As a hair stylist since 2012 - most recently as a Senior Stylist at JCPenney Salon and now as an independent stylist at Hot Headz Hair Salon - every appointment begins with a consultation:
listening carefully, asking the right questions, explaining options honestly, and following through. I manage my own scheduling, client records, reminders, and follow-up, and I am trusted daily with conversations people do not have with just anyone. 

Alongside that, my work as a cleaning technician has added reliability, discretion inside people's homes, and careful attention to detail. 

That people-first work also includes two years at Solterra Wellness Center, where I practiced as a certified Reiki III practitioner and wellness guide. There I supported clients one-on-one through grief, stress, and difficult life transitions - listening without judgment, explaining each step of the process, and helping people feel grounded and cared for in moments when they felt anything but. Holding a safe, steady space for someone in a vulnerable moment - staying present, unhurried, and calm while they process - is a skill I have practiced deliberately, and I consider it central to my work. It deepened the same skills this role calls for: a calm presence, clear communication, confidentiality, and genuine respect for wherever a person is starting from.

As a parent myself, I understand that when a family contacts an admissions team, they are often scared,
overwhelmed, and looking for someone who will treat them with patience and respect. That is the part of
this role I would take most seriously: answering questions clearly, keeping information organized and
confidential, coordinating next steps, and making sure no family feels lost in the process. I am comfortable
working remotely, learning new systems, and communicating by phone, video, and email, and I bring a steady, nonjudgmental presence to sensitive conversations.

I would welcome the chance to bring that experience to your admissions team and to the families you
serve. Thank you for your time and consideration.

Warmly,
Theresa Marie Therrien

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to express my interest in the Remote Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a bachelor’s degree in Human Services, concentrating in Psychology, and professional experience in behavioral health, forensic case management, and child welfare services, I bring a strong understanding of the complexities individuals and families face when navigating mental health and treatment services.

In my current role as a Forensic Specialist with IBIS Healthcare, I coordinate care for individuals with complex behavioral health needs, communicate with treatment providers and community partners, facilitate referrals, monitor placement progress, and navigate systems involving inpatient, residential, and community-based services. This experience has strengthened my ability to manage multiple cases, communicate effectively with diverse populations, maintain detailed documentation, and advocate for appropriate levels of care.

My background in child welfare and behavioral health has also given me a strong appreciation for the importance of family involvement, trauma-informed communication, and timely access to treatment. I understand that seeking mental health or substance use treatment for an adolescent can be an overwhelming and emotional experience for families. I would approach each admissions interaction with empathy, professionalism, and a commitment to helping families feel informed, supported, and confident throughout the process.

I am particularly interested in this opportunity because it would allow me to combine my professional background, education, and passion for behavioral health advocacy in a remote setting. I am confident that my experience with referrals, care coordination, documentation, and multidisciplinary communication would allow me to make a meaningful contribution to your admissions team.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my qualifications and experience align with the needs of Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Sincerely,

Jess

Sincerely,

Kyesha Devone

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With my background in healthcare, caregiving, customer service, and administrative support, combined with my personal connection to the challenges of addiction, I am passionate about the opportunity to help adolescents and their families access the care and support they deserve.

Growing up with a mother who struggled with addiction, I witnessed firsthand the emotional impact substance use can have on individuals and their families. Those experiences shaped me into a compassionate, understanding, and resilient person. They also taught me the importance of having someone who listens without judgment, offers reassurance, and provides guidance during difficult times. I want to use my personal experiences to make a positive difference in the lives of others, especially young people who may be struggling to find hope and stability.

Throughout my professional career, I have developed strong communication, organizational, and interpersonal skills. My experience in healthcare and administrative roles has allowed me to work with individuals from diverse backgrounds, manage sensitive information, coordinate appointments, and provide compassionate support. My caregiving experience has further strengthened my patience, empathy, and ability to respond to individual needs with professionalism and respect.

I understand that reaching out for mental health or substance use treatment can be an overwhelming and emotional experience for both adolescents and their families. I would welcome the opportunity to be that first reassuring voice, helping families navigate the admissions process while ensuring they feel heard, supported, and respected.

I am dependable, detail-oriented, comfortable with technology, and eager to learn. More importantly, I have a genuine desire to help others and turn my personal experiences into something meaningful. I would be proud to contribute to the mission of Adolescent Wellness Academy and help families take that important first step toward healing and recovery.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my personal experiences, professional background, and passion for helping others would make me a valuable addition to your team.

Sincerely,

Morgan Traxler

Application for: Virtual Admissions Coordinator 

Dear Hiring Team at Adolescent Wellness Academy,

 I am writing to express my strong interest in joining Adolescent Wellness Academy (AWA) as a remote Admissions Coordinator. With eight years of hands-on behavioral and mental health experience—2 of those years remote only -including five years as a Registered Behavior Technician (RBT) working across all age groups and three years in inpatient psychiatric hospital admissions—I am deeply drawn to AWA’s mission of providing compassionate, family-centered mental health and substance use support for teens and their families.
In my three years handling admissions at an inpatient mental health hospital, I frequently served as the first point of contact for individuals and families navigating acute behavioral health crises. That role required calm crisis de-escalation, thorough initial assessments under pressure, and clear, empathetic communication with both distressed families and multidisciplinary clinical teams. Because AWA’s virtual admissions and program teams guide parents and teens through pivotal moments toward PHP and IOP care, my background in high-acuity intake, compliance, and smooth care transitions directly prepares me to support families from their very first call.
Additionally, my five years as an RBT working across every developmental stage—from early childhood through adolescence and adulthood—have given me a strong ability to build rapport with teenagers and adjust my communication style to meet them where they are. In that role, I consistently maintained precise digital session documentation, tracked behavioral data, and collaborated remotely with supervisors and families to support individualized care plans. Working across both outpatient behavioral programs and acute inpatient settings has made me highly adaptable, self-directed, and comfortable managing sensitive workflows in a remote environment.
I admire how AWA bridges clinical excellence with genuine warmth so teens feel heard, understood, and supported alongside their families. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my admissions background and adolescent behavioral experience can contribute to your virtual team. Thank you for your time and consideration.

Sincerely,
Janae Tate

Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

After spending the last decade working in education, I've realized that some of the most meaningful parts of my job have had very little to do with teaching. It's been the relationships I've built with families, the difficult conversations we've navigated together, and the opportunities I've had to make someone feel heard and supported.

I'm currently finishing my bachelor's degree in Psychology and plan to pursue a master's in School Counseling. Mental health and substance use recovery are both areas I care deeply about, which is why this position immediately caught my attention.

I understand how difficult asking for help can be, and I would be grateful for the opportunity to make that first step a little easier for someone.

Thank you so much for your time and consideration. I would love the opportunity to be part of your team!

Warmly,
Shannon Urban

I’m writing to express my interest in joining Adolescent Wellness Academy. My experience in residential youth care, peer support, and crisis intervention has taught me how to build trust with young people, provide consistent structure, and stay calm when situations escalate.
At ACES Youth Home, I led a shift team of seven child care workers supporting up to ten adolescents in residential care. I supervised daily routines, maintained case documentation, and used trauma-informed de-escalation to help residents manage difficult moments. I also led weekly life-skills groups, where I helped young people practice coping strategies, work through conflict, and make decisions they could feel good about.
As Director of a Peer Support and Wellness Center, I strengthened my ability to connect with people facing mental health and substance use challenges. Later, as a Jail Reentry Specialist with the Cherokee County Sheriff’s Office, I developed individualized service plans, facilitated groups on recovery and anger management, and coordinated with treatment providers and community partners. Those roles reinforced the importance of listening carefully, setting clear expectations, and following through on commitments.
I would welcome the opportunity to bring that same steady, respectful approach to your team and help adolescents build skills they can use at home, at school, and in their relationships. Thank you for considering my application. I’d appreciate the chance to discuss how my experience could support the young people in your program.
Sincerely,
Danny Lee Greene

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position supporting your adolescent mental health and substance use treatment programs. What immediately drew me to this opportunity is the importance of being the first person someone encounters when they are reaching out for help. I would value the opportunity to bring my communication, coordination, administrative, and people-management experience to a role where those skills can make a meaningful difference.

Throughout my career, I have worked in positions requiring strong communication, organization, discretion, and the ability to remain composed when dealing with challenging situations. As the owner and operator of a remodeling business, I was responsible for managing customers, employees, subcontractors, schedules, finances, payroll, HR administration, and competing priorities simultaneously. I learned how important it is to listen carefully, ask the right questions, communicate clearly, and follow through on what people need.

My experience has also given me a strong administrative foundation. I have handled detailed documentation, data entry, electronic records, invoicing, payroll, HR administration, and customer communication. In my most recent industrial role, I worked with Procore and Excel to maintain project documentation and reviewed paperwork for accuracy and organization.

I am also currently pursuing undergraduate studies in Forensic Psychology and Business Management.  I am especially interested in opportunities where I can combine my professional experience with my growing understanding of people, communication, and human behavior.

I understand that someone contacting a treatment program may be reaching out during an extremely difficult moment. I would approach every interaction with patience, compassion, professionalism, and respect while helping the individual or family understand the next steps available to them. I am comfortable learning new systems and procedures, handling sensitive information appropriately, and coordinating details to ensure that people do not feel lost in the process.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my work ethic, life experience, organizational strengths, and genuine desire to help people to your team. Thank you for considering my application. I would be grateful for the opportunity to discuss how my background could contribute to your admissions team.

Sincerely,

Shauna Ballard

Dear Hiring Team,

I'm applying for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. When someone calls a treatment program, they are often scared and unsure of what to do next. I want to be the person who answers with warmth and gets them to a clear next step.

I currently work in two roles. At Engaging Thoughts Counseling, I support the VP of Compliance and work with the Clinical Director and clinical staff on HIPAA documentation, confidential records, and compliance reporting. This is my daily work in a behavioral health setting. It has taught me to handle sensitive information carefully and to manage my own calendar and deadlines without daily direction. At the American Red Cross, I coordinate intake appointments, answer incoming calls, register clients, and follow up. I also keep confidential client profiles and send weekly reports to regional leadership.

My background fits the core of this role:
- **Calls and follow-up:** At Family Care Management, I managed client registration, intake documentation, scheduling, and multi-line phone inquiries for more than three years. At Universal Orlando, I helped 150+ people a day with sensitive requests and used Salesforce CRM to verify accounts and track every follow-up.
- **Bilingual and trained in psychology:** I'm fluent in English and Spanish, and I hold a B.A. in Psychology. I can explain next steps plainly to a teen's parent or an adult in crisis, in the language they're most comfortable in.
- **Documentation and compliance:** I know HIPAA expectations well, and I'm careful about tracking every lead and conversation accurately.

I haven't yet worked in a treatment center's admissions department, and I won't pretend otherwise. I do bring the skills this role depends on: calm phone presence, consistent follow-up, accurate records, and respect for confidentiality. I learn systems quickly. I did it with Salesforce, and I would approach Kipu and insurance verification the same way. I'm available Monday through Friday, full-time, and ready to work independently from home.

Thank you for your time. I would welcome the chance to talk about how I can support your admissions team and the families who call you.

Sincerely,
Anthony Martinez

Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. Most recently, I have worked with younger children and families navigating mental health challenges, developmental disabilities, and other sensitive personal circumstances. These experiences have given me a deep appreciation for the importance of compassionate care, patient communication, and reliable support during some of life's most challenging moments. I believe my combination of administrative experience, intake, mental health trainings and genuine commitment to helping others would allow me to make a meaningful contribution to your team.

In my most recent role supporting an Early Childhood Intervention program, I facilitated referrals, coordinated evaluations, managed medical records, and handled a high volume of incoming calls. I worked closely with families and team members to help ensure individuals received the services and resources they needed. 

My responsibilities also included maintaining accurate records, performing data entry, coordinating office needs, and managing a variety of administrative tasks that help keep daily operations running smoothly. Additionally, my training in HIPAA, mental health-related topics and other areas has reinforced the importance of confidentiality, professionalism, and treating every individual with dignity and respect.

Whether answering a call, coordinating an appointment, managing sensitive information, or helping someone connect with appropriate resources, I recognize the importance of making people feel heard, respected, and supported.

My experience across different age groups and care settings has given me a broad perspective, adaptability, and a strong understanding of the importance of individualized support. I am comfortable balancing multiple responsibilities, collaborating with colleagues, and recognizing the importance of both efficient administrative processes and meaningful human connection.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience, dedication, and compassionate approach to service align with the needs of the Adolescent Wellness Academy team. I look forward to the possibility of contributing to your mission and supporting the patients and families who rely on your services.

Warm regards,

Jorge Ruiz

Dear Hiring Manager:
I am writing to express my interest in opportunities where I can apply my background in behavioral health, client
services, education, and community-based work. With more than four years of experience across psychiatric,
hospital, educational, and youth-focused settings, I have developed a strong foundation in direct care, behavioral
support, communication, documentation, and service coordination.
As a Registered Behavior Technician, I currently provide individualized ABA interventions for children ages 2–9
with autism spectrum disorder. My work includes tracking behavioral data, reviewing treatment responses,
identifying patterns, and using de-escalation strategies when needed. Previously, in an acute psychiatric setting, I
supported children, adolescents, and adults during high-stress situations. I also documented behavioral changes
and communicated observations to interdisciplinary teams to support treatment planning and continuity of care.
Together, these experiences have strengthened my ability to work carefully, remain composed, and respond to
individual needs in structured service environments.
My background also extends into education, youth programming, hospital-based child services, and coaching. I
have worked with children ranging from infancy through age 10, adapted activities to different developmental and
skill levels, and maintained clear communication with families, teachers, and colleagues. These roles strengthened
my ability to build rapport, adjust quickly, and create structure while working with people who may have very
different needs and communication styles.
Academically, I hold a B.A. in Psychology and am currently pursuing a Master of Social Work. My studies have
included research methods, behavioral and clinical psychology, human development, social determinants of
health, and behavioral change. This foundation complements my hands-on experience and supports my interest in
roles involving client services, care coordination, research support, community programs, and other people-
centered work.
In addition, my background as a former NCAA student-athlete has shaped how I approach teamwork,
accountability, and performance. Competing at the collegiate level while earning academic recognition required
discipline, adaptability, and consistent follow-through in demanding environments. Those same strengths continue
to inform how I contribute professionally.
I would welcome the opportunity to bring this combination of behavioral health experience, communication skills,
analytical thinking, and service-focused work to your organization. Thank you for your time and consideration.
Sincerely,
Jadyn Chee

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team,

I recently applied for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position and wanted to share why this work
matters to me. When a parent calls about mental health or substance use treatment for their teen, they
may be worried and unsure where to start. I’d like to be the person who listens, explains the next step
clearly, and follows through on what I said I would do.

At True North Pediatrics, I helped families with patient intake, scheduling, referrals, and insurance
verification. I kept patient records up to date and followed up when information was missing. As a
Child Protective Investigator with the Florida Department of Children and Families, I spoke with
children and caregivers during difficult circumstances and documented sensitive information with
care. Both roles taught me how much it matters to stay calm, ask clear questions, and make sure
families know what happens next.
I’m fluent in English and Spanish, and I’ve supported clients by phone, email, and video. My studies in
forensic psychology and my training as a Christian Mental Health Coach have deepened my interest in
how families navigate the decision to seek help.

I’d bring that perspective to your admissions team along with the practical habits I’ve built in pediatric care: keeping track of referrals, protecting confidential information, and following up when a family is waiting for an answer.

Thank you for considering my application. I’d welcome the opportunity to talk with you about how I can support your admissions team and the families who reach out to Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Sincerely,
Lizmar Encarnacion-Rosario

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With a bachelor's degree in Psychology, ongoing graduate studies in Social Work, and professional experience in behavioral health intake, case management, and substance use support, I bring a combination of clinical understanding, administrative coordination, and compassionate communication. As a bilingual English- and Spanish-speaking professional, I am especially passionate about helping individuals and families overcome barriers to accessing mental health and substance use treatment.

In my current role as a Case Manager at EMC Behavioral, I work in a fully virtual environment, supporting children and adolescents experiencing mental health and substance use challenges. My responsibilities include conducting intake assessments, identifying service needs, verifying insurance, coordinating referrals, scheduling appointments, and maintaining accurate client documentation. Working remotely has strengthened my ability to independently manage my responsibilities, communicate effectively with clients and caregivers through virtual platforms, and ensure timely follow-up without requiring daily in-person supervision. I understand the importance of maintaining confidentiality, accurate documentation, and consistent communication when coordinating behavioral health services remotely.

Additionally, as a Bilingual Parent Support Specialist at Catholic Charities' Guadalupe Home, I support young mothers experiencing various challenges, including substance use concerns, in a residential shelter environment. My work involves providing trauma-informed support, assisting with behavioral and emotional challenges, communicating with residents, and maintaining accurate documentation. Working with individuals during vulnerable periods has taught me the importance of approaching difficult conversations with empathy, patience, and professionalism while helping individuals feel respected and supported.

I am particularly drawn to this opportunity because both programs serve populations with whom I have direct professional experience. I understand that individuals and families seeking behavioral health or substance use treatment may feel overwhelmed, uncertain, or afraid. I believe that providing clear information, listening without judgment, and following through on next steps can make a meaningful difference in their willingness and ability to access care. My experience with insurance verification, intake coordination, appointment scheduling, and client communication, combined with my ability to work independently in a fully remote environment, aligns closely with the responsibilities of this position.

I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my behavioral health experience, organizational skills, and bilingual communication abilities to your admissions team. Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background can support your programs and the individuals and families you serve.

Sincerely,
Jennyfer Alvidrez

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

I am excited to have the opportunity to apply to Adolescent Wellness Academy. Your mission to create a safe, compassionate, and supportive environment for adolescents facing mental health challenges aligns closely with my values, education, and experience. I am passionate about helping others feel seen, heard, and valued, and I welcome the opportunity to contribute to a team making a meaningful difference in young people's lives.

I hold a bachelor's degree in Psychology with a minor in Family Science and am currently pursuing a master's degree in Clinical Mental Health Counseling. I have four years of experience as a Registered Behavior Technician, providing one-on-one support to children and adolescents up to age 18 on the autism spectrum in home and clinical settings. In this role, I implemented evidence-based interventions, monitored client progress through data collection, and maintained a safe, supportive environment. As an Intervention Specialist, I also supported elementary-aged students with their academic, behavioral, and individual needs.

Beyond my direct experience working with children, I have developed strong leadership, communication, and organizational skills. In my role leading volunteer operations for my church, I had the privilege of training and supervising more than 30 volunteers a day, ranging in age from 18 to 98. Working with such a diverse group taught me the importance of humility, adaptability, active listening, and recognizing different learning styles. I worked to create an inclusive environment where every individual felt heard and valued while helping improve daily operations through collaboration and individualized training. I also provided administrative support by answering phones, assisting visitors, responding to questions, and coordinating schedules.

I am drawn to Adolescent Wellness Academy because of your commitment to connection, compassion, and individualized care. I believe one of the most meaningful things we can offer is a place where individuals feel safe to be themselves and know they are not alone and that they have value and purpose. 

Thank you for considering my application. I would be grateful for the chance to join your team and support the important work you do.

Sincerely, Kaley Rhoton

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a background in management, healthcare, rehabilitation, and administrative operations, I believe I bring a unique combination of leadership experience, compassion, strong communication skills, and the ability to work independently that would make me a strong addition to your team.

Throughout my career, I have worked in environments where compassion, professionalism, attention to detail, and the ability to navigate challenging situations are essential. My experience working in drug and alcohol rehabilitation gave me exposure to the importance of supportive care and the impact that treatment can have on individuals and families. I understand that reaching out for help can be overwhelming, and I would approach every interaction with patience, empathy, respect, and a genuine desire to help people navigate the next steps in accessing care.

Most recently, I served as a Shelter Clinic Manager, where I was responsible for overseeing daily operations, supervising and developing employees, coordinating workflows, managing purchasing and budgets, maintaining compliance, developing policies and procedures, and resolving operational challenges. My management experience has strengthened my ability to multitask, prioritize competing demands, maintain accurate documentation, communicate effectively, and follow through on responsibilities. I am comfortable learning new systems, working with sensitive information, and maintaining professionalism in fast-paced environments where accuracy and organization are critical.

I also bring experience working in hybrid and remote environments and am confident in my ability to manage my workload independently while remaining communicative, dependable, and accountable. I am proactive about staying organized, following through on outstanding tasks, managing deadlines, and ensuring that nothing falls through the cracks. I understand that remote work requires discipline, initiative, strong time management, and the ability to take ownership of your responsibilities, all of which I have developed throughout my management career.

I am particularly drawn to this opportunity because it combines healthcare, meaningful human connection, organization, and the opportunity to make a difference in someone’s life. I am looking to transition my management and healthcare experience into a role where I can continue supporting others while contributing my administrative, communication, and operational strengths. I would be grateful for the opportunity to bring my experience, work ethic, compassion, and dedication to your team.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background and skills could contribute to the success of Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Bailey Jallo, CVT

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With a Specialized Associate’s Degree in Medical Assisting, extensive experience in healthcare administration and patient coordination, and over 15 years of customer service experience, I believe I bring a strong combination of medical knowledge, communication skills, and compassion that would make me an asset to your admissions team.

Throughout my healthcare career, I have worked in several specialty settings, including pain management, and wellness. My experience includes coordinating patient appointments and referrals, communicating with patients and providers, maintaining electronic medical records, handling confidential health information, and helping patients navigate the next steps in their care. I am familiar with EMR systems, Athena, medical terminology, HIPAA compliance, and the importance of accurate documentation and timely follow-up.

I understand that the admissions process is often someone’s first interaction with a healthcare organization, and that first impression matters. My background in both healthcare and customer service has taught me how to actively listen, establish trust, navigate sensitive conversations, and communicate information in a way that makes people feel comfortable and understood. My caregiving experience has further strengthened my patience, compassion, and ability to support individuals and families through challenging circumstances.

I am particularly drawn to this opportunity because of the meaningful work your programs provide to adolescents and adults seeking mental health and substance use treatment. I recognize that reaching out for help can be overwhelming, both for individuals and their loved ones. I would take that responsibility seriously by approaching every inquiry with empathy, professionalism, discretion, and a commitment to helping each caller find an appropriate next step.

I am organized, adaptable, self-motivated, and comfortable managing multiple responsibilities in fast paced environments. I understand the importance of maintaining accurate lead records, following up consistently, coordinating documentation, and ensuring that no inquiry falls through the cracks. I am confident in my ability to learn new systems and processes quickly while maintaining a high standard of patient communication and organization.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my healthcare background, administrative experience, and genuine passion for helping others to your growing team. Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to discussing how my qualifications could contribute to your admissions department.

Sincerely,

Christine Cushley

Dear Hiring Team,

I’m applying for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. I enjoy being the person families can turn to when they know they need help and are trying to figure out where to start. This role brings together the work I’ve done in behavioral health intake, insurance verification, and supporting people seeking mental health and substance use treatment.

As a Bilingual Care Coordinator at Cartwheel Health, I was one of the first people students and families spoke with when starting services. I explained the intake process in English and Spanish, answered questions, coordinated appointments with clinicians and school teams, and followed up with families about next steps. In my current role as an Eligibility Specialist, I verify benefits, review documentation, and help families work through coverage issues that could delay care. Both roles have taught me how to keep multiple intakes moving remotely while giving each family the time and attention they need.

During my clinical internship at Catholic Charities in Trenton, I supported adolescents in the New Choices Program and adults in the Project Free intensive outpatient substance use program. I conducted intake assessments under supervision, facilitated groups, and coordinated referrals. That experience gave me a better understanding of what people may be going through when they make that first call and how much a calm conversation and a clear next step can help.

Thank you for considering my application. I’d welcome the opportunity to bring my bilingual communication skills, intake experience, and follow-through to your admissions team.

Sincerely,
Stephany Bhisham

November 24, 2026

Adolescent Wellness Academy Talent Acquisition Team

RE: Program Director – Virtual IOP | Adolescent Behavioral Health

Dear Hiring Committee:

Adolescent Wellness Academy’s virtual IOP requires a leader who can balance clinical quality with the operational discipline to grow access, sustain census and build trusted referral relationships. My experience spans behavioral health program startup, executive healthcare operations, telehealth service delivery and national child and family services, positioning me to help expand a high-quality virtual program for adolescents and their families.

As Director of Residential Treatment Facilities at Concept Health Systems, I launched a newly licensed behavioral health program and built the staffing, policies, partnerships and workflows required for sustainable operations. I directed multidisciplinary services, budgeting, licensing, accreditation and workforce development, independently securing partnerships for medication-assisted treatment, pharmacy services and integrated medical care. The program maintained 100% occupancy for 33 of 36 months, including throughout the pandemic.

At Optum, I delivered behavioral health services in a large-scale telehealth environment, applying evidence-based approaches to engagement and care coordination. I ranked among the top-performing providers based on performance analytics, participant satisfaction and program success measures. That direct virtual-care experience informs how I would support clinical teams, monitor engagement and strengthen the participant experience in a virtual IOP.

At Urban Strategies, as Assistant Program Director and Interim Director, I helped scale an ORR child and family services program nationwide, developing standardized processes, specialty-service structures and quality controls. My earlier school assessment, truancy court and child advocacy work also provides a practical understanding of the systems surrounding adolescents and their caregivers.

I would bring AWA a growth-oriented approach to school and provider outreach, referral conversion, census forecasting, staffing coverage, audit readiness and leadership reporting, working closely with licensed clinical leaders on treatment quality. Based in Tampa, I welcome the opportunity to help build a sustainable virtual IOP that expands access to timely, family-centered behavioral healthcare across Florida.

Sincerely,
Chantel George, M.Ed.

Dear Hiring Committee,

I am writing to express my interest in the Program Director position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a Master of Science in Clinical Mental Health Counseling from Barry University, a Bachelor of Science in Psychology from Florida A&M University, and professional experience spanning behavioral health quality assurance, team supervision, program leadership, and psychological research, I bring a multidisciplinary perspective to clinical program development and leadership.

My professional background has allowed me to develop an understanding of behavioral health services from both clinical and operational perspectives. In my current capacity as a Mental Health Quality Assurance Specialist and Supervisor, I oversee a team while supporting clinical quality, documentation standards, regulatory compliance, and continuous improvement. This experience has strengthened my ability to evaluate clinical processes, support staff accountability, identify opportunities for improvement, and maintain standards that promote safe, ethical, and effective care. I understand that successful behavioral health programming requires more than quality clinical services; it requires intentional leadership, operational consistency, and a commitment to measurable outcomes.

Additionally, my leadership experience in a museum setting has strengthened my ability to coordinate people, support organizational objectives, and engage with diverse communities. These experiences, combined with my behavioral health background, have shaped my approach to leadership as one grounded in collaboration, communication, accountability, and relationship-building.

My academic and research experiences have further informed my commitment to culturally responsive and family-centered mental health services. Through my graduate training and international research experience in Bali, Indonesia, I explored the intersections of cultural identity, spirituality, resilience, social support, and psychological well-being. These experiences reinforced the importance of understanding individuals within their broader family, cultural, and social environments. I am particularly interested in ensuring that adolescents and their families have access to mental health services that recognize their individual needs while addressing the systems and circumstances that influence their well-being.

I am especially drawn to Adolescent Wellness Academy’s family-centered approach and its commitment to providing structured behavioral health services to adolescents. The opportunity to contribute to the growth of a virtual Intensive Outpatient Program is exciting because it brings together several areas of my professional interests: clinical quality, program leadership, community engagement, team development, and accessible mental health care.

I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my clinical knowledge, supervisory experience, research perspective, and commitment to organizational excellence to AWA. I am confident that my interdisciplinary background would allow me to bring a thoughtful, collaborative, and quality-driven approach to the continued development of your Virtual IOP.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience and professional goals align with Adolescent Wellness Academy’s mission.

Sincerely,

Gabriela C. Sevrin, M.S.
