Dear AWA Hiring Team,

I am excited to apply for the Program Director, Virtual IOP – Adolescent Behavioral Health position. I have worked with a few of you closely already! As a licensed therapist with over 10 years of experience in behavioral healthcare, including serving as Director of Admissions at Galen Hope, I bring a unique combination of clinical expertise, operational leadership, and a genuine passion for improving access to quality mental health treatment.

Throughout my career, I have worked extensively with adolescents and families navigating complex mental health challenges, including anxiety, depression, eating disorders, and co-occurring conditions. I understand that a successful virtual IOP requires more than strong clinical programming; it requires an engaged team, efficient systems, meaningful family collaboration, and an environment where adolescents feel supported and connected, even through a screen.

I pride myself on being an approachable, collaborative, and solutions-oriented leader who values both clinical excellence and the people responsible for delivering it. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, energy, and commitment to adolescent mental health to AWA, helping strengthen and grow a program that makes meaningful treatment accessible to more families.

Warm regards,

Chloe Godward

candidates.summary:
I am a behavioral health executive with over a decade of progressive leadership experience developing, scaling, and overseeing clinical programs across the full continuum of care, including residential treatment, PHP, IOP, and outpatient services. As Senior Clinical Director for Caron Treatment Centers in Florida, I oversee multidisciplinary teams, clinical operations, program budgets, revenue and expense targets, regulatory compliance, and performance improvement initiatives. My leadership has contributed to expanding treatment capacity from startup to 75 beds within months while supporting programs serving more than 500 patients annually.

At Hazelden Betty Ford, I spearheaded the development and implementation of English and Spanish virtual behavioral health services in just two weeks during the pandemic, establishing telehealth infrastructure, clinical workflows, and standardized curriculum across multiple markets. I also developed specialized outpatient programming and led efforts to standardize service delivery across locations nationwide.

My experience combines clinical excellence with business strategy, including census growth, operational efficiency, financial performance, staff development, EHR optimization, and regulatory readiness. I bring a demonstrated ability to build sustainable programs, lead high-performing teams, strengthen access to care, and deliver exceptional patient and family experiences.

candidates.cover_letter:
To whom it may concern,
My name is Selena, and I am excited to be applying for the primary therapist position at North Carolina's first-ever AWA location! I am an LCSWA with multiple years of experience providing therapeutic support in numerous capacities, including as a behavioral health technician, case manager, and psychotherapist. I've also gained experience in a diverse range of therapeutic settings, such as an inpatient adolescent hospital, PHP/IOP mental health clinics, community health (including in-home), and outpatient therapy. The most influential experiences I've gained have been working in adolescent inpatient and PHP/IOP clinics, in which I became comfortable leading group therapy sessions, providing 1:1 individual therapy as well as family-based therapy, and working collaboratively with clinical teams consisting of numerous disciplines and treatment goals. I've also become comfortable with higher levels of care, which I am able to use to offer clients validation and unconditional positive regard, as these experiences can be exhausting. In my current outpatient work, I primarily work with pre-teens and adolescents, as I witnessed a gap in care for these age groups despite the intensity of these transformative years. I aspire to be a supportive resource to these clients in whatever capacity I am able to, as it is already difficult to be a teen, let alone one who feels misunderstood and alone in the journey.

Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

I would welcome the opportunity to join Adolescent Wellness Academy in a role supporting teens. I hold a bachelor’s degree in psychology and bring 28 years of experience in mental health, including direct care and staff supervision in adolescent residential settings. What draws me to this work is seeing a young person begin to trust an adult enough to ask for help when they need it.

At Alexander Youth Network, I supported adolescents through daily routines, peer conflicts, and moments of crisis. Some of the most meaningful progress I saw happened before a situation escalated. When a young person recognized that a peer interaction was becoming overwhelming and came to me to ask to move, I reinforced that choice. As a house manager, I also helped staff recognize those early signs, document what they observed, and share which approaches helped so the next shift could provide consistent support.

At Nazareth Child & Family Connection, I worked with adolescents facing substance use concerns and the effects of trauma. That experience shaped how I build relationships. I listen to the young person’s account, explain expectations clearly, and follow through on what I say. I would bring that same patience, reliability, and respect to the teens and colleagues I work with at your academy.

Thank you for considering my application. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my experience in adolescent behavioral health could support your team.

Sincerely,
Kinda Rogers

I am excited to apply for the Bilingual Virtual Program Coordinator position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. As a Psychology graduate, I have been looking for an opportunity to work in a mental health setting where I can contribute to something meaningful while continuing to develop professionally. I enjoy remote work and the organization and communication that come with it, but what matters most to me is knowing that my work is helping people.

My interest in this field has grown even stronger since beginning my volunteer experience with the Alachua Crisis Center. It has reminded me how important it is to have people who are willing to listen, offer support, and help others through difficult moments. It has also made me realize how much I want my everyday work to be connected to making a difference in someone's life.

I previously worked at Nicaragua Recovery, a residential recovery program, where I supported patients through daily check-ins, activities, and recovery programming. I facilitated daily One Day at a Time reflection groups and translated the discussions into English for patients who did not speak Spanish so they could participate fully. I also interpreted conversations between patients and their outside caregivers, helping make communication easier and ensuring patients could better understand and express themselves. Later, I worked remotely as an Outreach Coordinator for the same program, contacting prospective patients, explaining the program, answering questions, and communicating with clinics and therapists about potential referrals.

In my current remote administrative position, I manage correspondence, organize information, communicate with customers, and coordinate with different departments. These responsibilities have strengthened my ability to stay organized, communicate clearly, and manage tasks independently. I would be excited to bring these skills into a mental health setting where the administrative work directly supports patients, families, and clinical teams.

As a native English and Spanish speaker with a degree in Psychology, I would value the opportunity to contribute to AWA's work with adolescents and their families. I am dependable, eager to learn, and genuinely motivated to build a career in a field where I can help others.

Thank you for considering my application. I would appreciate the opportunity to speak with you about how my background and motivation could contribute to your team.

In three years as a Medicare Agent at Providence Senior Care, I helped approximately 500 beneficiaries enroll in Medicare Advantage plans. I earned the office’s Most Compliant recognition and was named its top female agent two years in a row.
 
I held agent licenses and carrier appointments across more than 30 states and worked with carriers including Humana, UnitedHealthcare, Aetna, Cigna, and Wellcare. I supported Medicare beneficiaries, including people eligible for both Medicare and Medicaid, by reviewing their healthcare needs, checking whether their providers and prescription medications were covered, and comparing plan options available in their ZIP code. I also trained new agents on CRM workflows, the SunFire enrollment platform, and dialing tools including Enroll Here and Convoso.
 
At State Farm, I’ve continued to build my insurance sales and customer service experience by managing opportunities in ECRM, explaining coverage, bundling auto and home policies, binding coverage, and assisting customers with billing and payment questions. I hold Florida 2-15 Life and Health and 4-40 Resident Customer Representative licenses and earned a bachelor’s degree in Health Science, magna cum laude, from Florida Atlantic University.
 
I’d welcome the opportunity to discuss how my Medicare enrollment, consultative sales, and compliance experience can support your team’s goals. Thank you for your consideration.

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in a counseling position within your organization. As a Licensed Mental Health Counselor and School Counselor, I bring a strong background in mental health counseling, student support, behavioral and emotional development, and the implementation of therapeutic interventions designed to promote personal growth and overall well-being.

My professional experience includes providing individual counseling, conducting emotional and behavioral assessments, developing treatment goals, and utilizing evidence-based therapeutic approaches to address concerns such as anxiety, depression, trauma, grief, self-esteem, emotional regulation, and interpersonal relationships. I am experienced in building therapeutic relationships, facilitating meaningful conversations, and creating supportive environments where individuals feel heard, respected, and empowered.

My background in school counseling has also strengthened my ability to identify students’ academic, social, emotional, and behavioral needs while collaborating with families, educators, and other professionals to promote student success. I value a person-centered approach and recognize the importance of meeting individuals where they are while helping them develop practical coping strategies and skills for long-term growth.

I am compassionate, dependable, and committed to maintaining professional and ethical standards while delivering quality counseling services. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my clinical knowledge, counseling experience, and dedication to your organization.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my qualifications and professional experience align with your organization’s needs.

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in a Mental Health Technician position with your organization. I hold a Bachelor of Arts in Psychology from Florida International University and am currently pursuing a master's degree in Clinical Mental Health Counseling at the University of the Cumberlands. With over five years of experience supporting clinical education at the University of Miami, I am eager to apply my academic background, interpersonal skills, and professional experience in a setting where I can contribute directly to the care and well-being of individuals experiencing mental health challenges.

In my current position as a Standardized Patient Lead at the University of Miami, I coordinate clinical simulation activities, collaborate with healthcare educators and learners, and help ensure that medical training encounters are conducted consistently and professionally. My work as a standardized patient has also involved portraying a variety of clinical scenarios, observing patient-provider interactions, documenting clinical communication and examination behaviors, and providing structured feedback to healthcare learners. These experiences have strengthened my communication, observation, adaptability, and documentation skills, while reinforcing the importance of empathy, confidentiality, and professionalism in healthcare environments.

My education in psychology and ongoing graduate counseling coursework have further developed my understanding of human behavior, mental health, and the importance of individualized, compassionate support. I am particularly interested in gaining hands-on experience within behavioral health settings, where I can learn from experienced professionals while contributing to a safe, supportive, and respectful environment for patients.

I recognize that working in mental health care requires patience, emotional awareness, dependability, and the ability to remain composed in challenging situations. I am committed to developing the practical skills necessary to meet these responsibilities and would welcome the opportunity to contribute to your team while continuing to grow professionally in the mental health field.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background, skills, and commitment to mental health care would make me a valuable addition to your organization.

Sincerely,
David Hernandez
